extracted.intended_audience: Canadian patent applicants, patent agents/attorneys, and patent examiners
extracted.subtask_short: drafting Canadian patent descriptions and claims
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and formal substantive requirements for preparing the description, drawings, amendments and claims of a Canadian patent application under the Patent Act and Patent Rules. Covers content, format, support, clarity, amendments, and examiner objection bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description must be correctly and fully disclosed
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention must be “correctly and fully” described in the description, which according to subsection 1(1) of the Patent Rules is “the part of the specification other than the claims”.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must be fully supported by the description (section 60 Patent Rules). A description that states the nature of the invention only by reference to the claims is improper and suggests non‑compliance with subsection 27(3) of the Patent Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not describe the invention by reference to the claims
rubrics_metrics.description: It is improper for the description to state the nature of the invention by reference to the claims (e.g. “the problem ... is overcome through the method of claim 1”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such statements must be removed or replaced by explicit description; examples of unacceptable language are provided. Amending the description to include originally filed claim language in a non‑divisional application is permissible (subsection 38.2(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove statements dependent on foreign practice or law
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements whose correctness depends on foreign patent prosecution practices or laws may be inaccurate or confusing in Canadian context and must be removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: indicating an application is a continuation‑in‑part or divisional of a foreign document, or incorrect statements about foreign government rights—these may be treated as incorrect defects under subsection 27(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Description form per section 56 — required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The description must include, in manner and order: (a) short precise title (no trademark/coined/personal name); (b) technical field; (c) background art important for understanding/searching/examination; (d) description permitting understanding of technical problem and its solution; (e) concise description of figures; (f) at least one mode contemplated using examples if appropriate; (g) sequence listing if required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsection 56(2) allows different order if it aids understanding; headings like 'Summary' or 'Detailed Description of Preferred Embodiments' are permitted but broader claim support must be found elsewhere in the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of the invention must be stated in a short and precise manner and must not include a trademark, coined word or personal name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title should describe the invention itself (e.g. “flame‑retardant rigid polyurethane foam” acceptable; “foam” not). Office will consider title in description as correct title and update database at grant if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background art disclosure obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must describe the background art that, as far as is known to them, is important for the understanding, searching and examination of the invention (paragraph 56(1)(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relevant background art is identified during prosecution, applicant may introduce references/descriptions to the description within limits of section 38.2 and subsection 27(3); examiners generally should not object simply because later‑identified background art was not added.

rubrics_metrics.name: At least one mode or embodiment (if appropriate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph 56(1)(f) requires that, 'if appropriate', the applicant set forth at least one mode contemplated by the inventor for carrying out the invention using examples, with reference to drawings if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'If appropriate' is not discretionary for the applicant to decide; necessity depends on the case and the disclosure requirements of subsection 27(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings permitted but cannot limit support
rubrics_metrics.description: Headings such as 'Summary of the Invention' and 'Detailed Description of the Preferred Embodiments' are permitted in Canadian practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a heading suggests 'preferred embodiments', support for claims broader than those embodiments must be found in other descriptive parts satisfying subsection 27(3), including enablement and sound prediction support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pages and pagination formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Pages of the description, as part of the specification, must be numbered consecutively (subsection 50(1) Patent Rules) and no page of the description may contain the petition, abstract, drawings or claims; each must begin on a new page (section 49 Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formatting non‑compliance under sections 13, 47, 48 may be identified by examiners or support staff to expedite allowance; requisitioning compliance is permissible under PCT Article 27.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description must not contain drawings (but formulas/tables allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with section 51 of the Patent Rules, the description must not contain drawings but may contain chemical or mathematical formulae and tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chemical formulae may be graphical (structures). Formulae/tables may be presented sideways where aiding presentation (subsection 14(2)); otherwise pages upright. Graphical data (graphs, spectra) may be included in description and if submitted as drawings must meet section 59 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference characters consistency between drawings/specification/abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Any reference characters appearing on figures in the drawings, and only these reference characters, must be mentioned in the description (subsection 59(11)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a reference character is used for a feature, it must be the same throughout the abstract, specification and drawings; the same reference character cannot refer to different features (subsection 59(12)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of trademarks in application
rubrics_metrics.description: Any trademark mentioned in the abstract, specification or drawing must be identified as such (section 52 Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each trademark should be identified at least once, preferably at first appearance—examples: '(trademark)', '™', or an asterisk with footnote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of documents referenced in description
rubrics_metrics.description: A document referred to in the description must be available to the public, be fully identified, and must not be incorporated by reference (section 57 Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent documents should be identified by country/office code plus a publication/patent number; application numbers acceptable if document published. Non‑patent documents should include author, publication, year, volume/issue, pages, chapter title, publisher, ISBN if applicable. URLs are problematic unless content is fixed and reliably retrievable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to description — inclusion of originally filed claims language
rubrics_metrics.description: One amendment always permissible from 'new matter' standpoint is inclusion of the language of the originally filed claims in the description of a non‑divisional application originally filed in English or French.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General amendment guidance is in chapters 11 and 20; amendments may not add new matter and special attention is required when replacing restrictive language with permissive language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments must not introduce new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments that enlarge scope (e.g. changing 'must be' to 'preferably') or remove guidance that renders an invention operable under previously excluded conditions may be seen as adding new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deleting text can also amount to adding new matter if it expands operable scope. Making description self‑consistent when it already contains both permissive and restrictive language is generally acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments referencing prior art may introduce new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Introducing teachings from a prior art document into the description may, depending on circumstances, introduce new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If specific teachings in prior art are required to enable the invention or to support a sound prediction and it would not have been clear to the skilled person which teachings were necessary as of the claim date, including those teachings may add new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objections on description — subsection 27(3) vs specific rule bases
rubrics_metrics.description: Objections dealing with substantive sufficiency are presented under subsection 27(3) of the Patent Act, but where more specific authority exists that should be used instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defects under subsection 27(3) can range from severe sufficiency issues to minor clarity defects. Formatting or other minor problems should be identified under the specific related Patent Rules sections when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings requirement when invention can be illustrated
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions which can be illustrated by means of drawings shall be so illustrated in an application for a patent (subsection 27(5.1) Patent Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings clarify principles of construction rather than dimensions; must clearly show all parts and be without colouring (subsection 59(3)). Known devices may be illustrated by conventional symbols; minimal text permitted; blank blocks must be labelled; figures showing prior art should be labelled 'PRIOR ART'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings must include reference characters corresponding to specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Each drawing must include reference characters corresponding with those in the specification (subsection 27(5.2) Patent Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner may require further drawings or dispense with any; failure to reply in good faith within 3 months to a notice for further drawings may cause abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings must conform to Patent Rules sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever drawings are provided they must conform to the provisions of sections 46, 49 and 59 and subsections 14(2) and 47(2) of the Patent Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsection 56(2) allows reference to drawings before concise description when reference is to prior art drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to drawings — no new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification and any drawings furnished as part of an application may be amended before the patent is issued (subsection 38.2(1)), but drawings may not be amended to add new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed amendment procedures are in Chapters 11 and 20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs allowed when drawings not suitable
rubrics_metrics.description: When an invention does not admit illustration by drawings but does by photographs, applicant may furnish photographs that illustrate the invention (subsection 59(2) Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographs may contain colour (subsection 59(3)) but remain subject to other subsection 59 requirements; other ROs may convert colour photos to black & white which can lose detail and risk adding new matter if details are later added.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must define invention to provide public notice
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim must define the invention so a person skilled in the art will understand where they may and may not go without infringing; claims must be distinct and explicit (section 27(4) Patent Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must be novel (whole claimed subject‑matter not part of state of the art) and specify positively all elements/features necessary to ensure the result set forth in the description. Each claim must be a single sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim structure (preamble, transitional phrase, body)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims may be drafted to contain: preamble/introductory phrase, transitional phrase, and body (purview).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble identifies category; transitional phrase (e.g., 'comprising' vs 'consisting of') indicates open/closed recitation; body lists elements, steps, ingredients, or groups. Any form of claim conforming to section 27(4) and Patent Rules acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of claim construction — essential elements and specification as whole
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims are the starting point for construing a patent; essential elements must be determined and the specification construed as a whole. Analysis is from viewpoint of skilled person with a mind willing to understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to description allowed only to assist understanding of claim terms where terms have a unique meaning; cannot be used to vary claim scope. During examination claims may be amended to remove ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain meaning unless description defines term
rubrics_metrics.description: Language of claims is interpreted by giving each term its plain and usual meaning in the art unless it is clear from the description that a term in the claims is to be given a different meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can act as their own lexicographer but must make it clear; inadvisable to redefine terms contrary to well‑known meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity requirement — avoid ambiguity and multiple interpretations
rubrics_metrics.description: No speculation should be necessary to determine what is covered by each claim; wording should not be so flexible that several interpretations are possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim is indefinite when its precise limits are uncertain. Broadness alone does not make a claim indefinite. Use simple language if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antecedent basis rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When an element is referred to in definite terms without introduction previously, the claim is objectionable under section 27(4) (lack of proper antecedent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied antecedents permitted where the phrase by definition contains the missing antecedent (examples provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of imprecise or vague expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims should not include vague expressions such as 'thin', 'strong', 'if desired', 'about', 'preferably', etc., unless further defined in clear terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual lists commonly used imprecise terms and discusses context where they may be acceptable or indefinite (e.g., 'therapeutically effective amount', 'a major part'). Consider subsection 27(4) and section 60 when such terms appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative limitations caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims containing negative expressions ('not being...', 'not having...') may be objectionable because claims should generally set forth what the invention is rather than what it is not, unless no positive way exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dependent claims that negate features of a preceding claim and become broader are objectionable under subsection 63(4) of the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of claims — recite sufficient elements for operability
rubrics_metrics.description: To define the invention distinctly and explicitly, sufficient elements must be recited for operability; inventive features must appear in each claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: composition claims generally must define a minimum of two ingredients at least broadly; failure to do so can be objected to as indefinite under subsection 27(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Support requirement — claims fully supported by description
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim must be fully supported by the description as required by section 60 of the Patent Rules; characteristics of embodiments set forth in the claim must be fully set forth in the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terms used in claims and description must be used in the same sense. Matter in originally filed claims may be added to the description (except for divisional applications with further requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims should not rely on references to description/drawings except narrowly
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally not acceptable for a claim to contain reference to the description or drawings (subsection 62(1) Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: reference numerals in parentheses (subsection 62(2)) if claim otherwise complete; charts/graphs/tables or complex tests may be referred to if reproducing them in the claim is impractical; sequence listing and biological deposit identifiers may be referenced (subsections 62(3),(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of claims relative to disclosure — applicant may draft narrow claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim may be as narrow as the applicant wishes within the scope of the invention disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope must, however, remain supported and enabled by the disclosure.
